title: Game Changers : le rêve mondial de Gentle Mates s’effondre au bout du suspense
content:
Après leur exploit face à Shopify Rebellion Gold, les joueuses de Gentle Mates s’attendaient à retrouver les Américaines en grande finale. Mais c’est finalement KRÜ Blaze qui a créé la surprise dans le lower bracket, en éliminant les favorites de la compétition (3-1). Un adversaire particulièrement dangereux pour les Françaises, d’autant que les Sud-Américaines pouvaient compter sur le soutien du public de São Paulo.

M8 a pourtant parfaitement lancé les hostilités sur son choix de carte, Haven, avec une victoire autoritaire (13-5). Mais KRÜ Blaze a immédiatement répliqué sur Abyss (13-5), portée par une Nonee impressionnante sur Jett (25/13/2, 1.59 de rating). La troisième manche sur Sunset a ensuite donné lieu à un scénario complètement fou. Menées 10-2, les joueuses de Gentle Mates ont frôlé un comeback historique, notamment grâce à un 1v4 sensationnel de berryx. Après avoir arraché les prolongations, elles ont finalement cédé (12-14). Dos au mur, les Françaises ont trouvé les ressources pour égaliser sur Split (13-8), avec 21 éliminations au compteur pour leur capitaine Nami.

WTFFFFFFFFF BERRYYYYYYYXFOIPKEAHPOEAF pic.twitter.com/sP7f3o1dCQ

Tout s’est donc joué sur Ascent, une carte particulièrement favorable à la défense. Et c’est justement dans ce camp que KRÜ Blaze a rapidement pris les commandes. Menées 7-1, les Françaises ont réussi à limiter les dégâts avant le changement de côté (7-5). Mais une nouvelle défaite lors du pistol round, un exercice qui leur aura trop souvent fait défaut dans cette finale, a compliqué leur remontée. Safiaa a bien repoussé une première balle de match grâce à un énorme quadruplé, mais KRÜ Blaze a fini par conclure deux rounds plus tard (13-8), s’adjugeant le BO5 et le titre mondial (3-2).

M8 RÉSILIENCE PLUS QUE JAMAIS #M8WIN pic.twitter.com/ZtuFHD0e0I

Une défaite cruelle pour Gentle Mates, jusqu’ici invaincue dans la compétition. Pour sa première année sur la scène féminine de VALORANT, la structure de Squeezie, Brawks et Gotaga termine sur la deuxième marche du podium, avec 100 000 dollars de cashprize. Les joueuses quittent le Brésil avec des regrets, mais aussi de nombreuses raisons d’être fières. Elles auront notamment fait tomber Team Liquid, championnes du monde en titre, avant de réussir un comeback mémorable face à Shopify Rebellion, considérées comme les grandes favorites du tournoi.

title: Team Spirit ends Team Yandex’s dominant run to claim Dota 2 PARI Universe title
content:
The PARI Universe Grand Final delivered a shocking result as Team Spirit swept Team Yandex 3-0, denying them a single game win and claiming the tournament title.

After falling to the lower bracket against OG, Team Spirit fought their way past PARIVISION, Team Liquid, and GamerLegion to reach the Grand Final, where they shut down Team Yandex, who had remained undefeated since the group stage.

Team Spirit and Team Yandex have established themselves as two of the strongest teams in the modern Dota 2 scene. Since The International 2026, the two organizations have repeatedly gone head-to-head, starting with BLAST SLAM 8.

Both teams finished at the top of their respective groups during the PARI Universe group stage. However, Team Spirit had to take the longer route to the Grand Final after suffering an upset loss to OG. Despite dropping to the lower bracket, they fought their way back to the championship series and proved they could overcome some of the tournament’s toughest opponents.

Team Spirit eventually swept the Grand Final 3-0, although each game was closely contested and forced the three-time TI champions to fight for every victory. More importantly, they appeared to expose a weakness that other teams had struggled to exploit against Team Yandex: focusing their attacks on Ammar “ATF” Al-Assaf.

The series also showed that Team Spirit’s success does not depend solely on their star carry. Their other players stepped up when it mattered, particularly Denis “Larl” Sigitov with his Earthshaker in Game 1 and Bohdan “Batyuk” Batiuk with Enigma in Game 2 and Timbersaw in Game 3.

title: Wildcard book Singapore Major place as NRG miss out
content:
A 13-0 Nuke against BARCA settles the last Americas invite, and Wildcard’s final against 100 Thieves tonight decides Europe’s last place too.

Wildcard are going to the PGL Major Singapore . They beat BARCA 2-0 in the FiReSPORTS Last Chance semi-final in Buenos Aires on Sunday, 13-7 on Inferno and 13-0 on Nuke, and that locks up the ninth and final Americas invite, as first reported by Dust2.us . NRG and BESTIA are out of the race.

The North Americans join Liquid and M80 from their own scene. HLTV’s VRS projection counted Wildcard as clinched after the semi-final, up from 56% a day earlier. Valve publish the standings on 2 November.

SINGAPORE HERE WE COME🇸🇬 pic.twitter.com/LQVMA4E6Xa

BARCA picked Inferno, and Wildcard won both pistol rounds on it. They led 8-4 at the half and closed it out 13-7. Wildcard’s own Nuke pick was over almost before it started: 12-0 on the T side, and Jadan “HexT” Postma won a 1v2 in round 13 to finish the map and the series without BARCA scoring a round.

Ethan “reck” Serrano was the best player on the server, 28-15 with 90.9% KAST. In-game leader Nemanja “nEMANHA” Đukić added 29 kills at 100.7 ADR, the highest on the server. That came two days after HexT told Dust2 Brasil that nEMANHA and Sebastian “fr3nd” Kuśmierz had both lost their voices the day before the tournament, with the IGL at about 40%.

title: How to Get Zoro’s Three Sword Style in Fortnite

Zoro Three Sword Style has Epic rarity. Players get it by searching chests, and it can also appear as floor loot. Unlike the Gum-Gum Fruit, which spawns in random locations, this weapon mainly comes from chests.

There is no guaranteed chest location, so the drop depends on luck. You do not need to buy Zoro’s outfit to pick it up. The Zoro skin is set to reach the Item Shop on November 7.

The weapon is also in the Reload loot pool. It is the only melee weapon added to the Fortnite loot pool for Treasure Hunters.

title: Fortnite Pirate Shop Token: How to Get and Activate It
content:
Fortnite Pirate Shop Token rewards are now available in the Treasure Hunters mini season. The rare item lets players claim Item Shop cosmetics for free during two 14-day periods, one in 2026 and one in 2027. Players find it by opening Chests in Battle Royale, and every squad member receives it when one player finds one.

This guide explains how to get the Fortnite Pirate Shop Token, how to activate it, and what it includes. It also covers the main restrictions.

The Fortnite Pirate Shop Token is an extremely rare reward in the Fortnite Treasure Hunters mini season. The mini season launched on November 1, 2026, with update v43.00. It bridges Chapter 7 Season 4 and Chapter 8.

Each token gives two uses. One works in 2026 and the other in 2027. Each use lasts 14 days from the moment a player activates it, which adds up to 28 days of free Item Shop claims.

During an active period, players can claim items sold for V-Bucks in the Item Shop at no cost. Depending on what appears in the shop, the claimed cosmetics could be worth thousands of dollars. Epic Games has not revealed the odds of finding the token.

Players can get the token by opening Chests in Battle Royale during Treasure Hunters. A Chest can trigger a free reward for the squad. Most rewards are Gizmos. Cosmetics and Pirate Shop access are also possible, but the chance is very slim.

title: « On peut clairement gagner » : Caliste et la Karmine Corp n’ont pas peur de T1
content:
Pour sa première participation aux Worlds, Caliste disputera déjà les quarts de finale. Un accomplissement majeur pour le jeune ADC de la Karmine Corp, qui n’a pourtant pas l’intention de se contenter de ce résultat. Interrogé par Sjokz après la victoire contre Movistar KOI (2-0), le Français a affiché sa satisfaction : « Je suis très heureux de cette victoire et de la confiance que nous avons aujourd’hui. Je pense que le tirage était plutôt bon pour nous. Nous sommes une très bonne équipe, j’ai vraiment confiance en mes coéquipiers et je pense que nous pouvons aller loin. » Un optimisme partagé par Busio, particulièrement heureux de retrouver les quarts de finale des Worlds : « C’est un moment vraiment spécial d’être de retour ici, mais aussi de faire partie d’une équipe que je trouve incroyablement forte. »

QUALIFIÉS EN PLAYOFFS DES WORLDS 2026 ON VIENT D'EXPLOSER MKOI 2-0 POUR ALLER EN QUARTS DES WORLDS LES AMIS, C'EST BIEN RÉEL #KCORP BSAHTEK POUR NICE, NOUS ON PRÉFÈRE LES WORLDS @MovistarKOILoL pic.twitter.com/Qr9MIwV8jY

Cette confiance ne doit rien au hasard. Caliste est notamment revenu sur les difficultés rencontrées par la KC lors des playoffs du LEC, après une excellente saison régulière estivale. « Nous avons très mal joué en playoffs, c’était un peu honteux » , a-t-il reconnu au micro de Sjokz. Depuis, l’équipe s’est imposé une discipline de travail particulièrement exigeante, aussi bien en scrims que dans les discussions collectives. Le bootcamp effectué en Corée a également permis aux joueurs de progresser individuellement, de mieux comprendre la méta et de renforcer leur jeu d’équipe.

Au micro d’Ethan Cohen pour OTP, Caliste a également expliqué comment la KC adapte désormais son approche stratégique selon ses adversaires. Face à KOI, les Français savaient qu’ils pouvaient privilégier des compositions orientées vers les teamfights, notamment grâce à leur supériorité dans les affrontements collectifs. Une stratégie qui ne sera toutefois pas forcément applicable contre les meilleures équipes asiatiques, capables de prendre rapidement l’avantage sur les lanes. Pour le joueur français, il est donc essentiel de ne pas s’enfermer dans une seule lecture de la méta.

Mais surtout, Caliste refuse de fixer une limite aux ambitions de son équipe. « Personnellement, j’y crois dur comme fer qu’on peut aller au bout, on peut y aller, on peut gagner » , a-t-il assuré à OTP. Le Français sait néanmoins que la suite s’annonce redoutable : « Maintenant, on est vraiment dans le vif du sujet, ça va être des BO5 contre des grosses équipes. Il ne reste que les huit meilleures équipes du monde. » Sans se présenter comme favori, il reste convaincu que la KC peut rivaliser avec les cadors : « On est clairement capables d’aller les titiller, de les faire tomber, et on est une équipe qui est assez dangereuse. » Premier test grandeur nature vendredi 6 novembre face à T1, champion du monde en titre, avant une éventuelle demi-finale contre Dplus KIA ou Bilibili Gaming.

title: Pokémon UNITE World Champion Lists Worlds Trophy for $400K
content:
Junglebook, who won the first Pokémon UNITE World Championship with North American team BLVKHVND, has put his 2022 trophy up for sale with an asking price of $400,000. He posted the listing on X on 30 October, days after it emerged that UNITE will shut down in March 2027.

“For sale is the official World Champion Trophy from the 2022 Pokémon World Championships in London,” the post reads. “I earned this trophy myself by taking 1st Place in Pokémon Unite the very first year the game was included in the World Championships.”

The trophy shows a Pikachu holding a smaller trophy while standing on top of a Poké Ball. Junglebook describes it as being in pristine condition and says it has only been held by him, during the 2022 awards ceremony. He also says the price is not fixed and that he is open to trades, including high-end graded Pokémon cards, as Dexerto reported .

For sale is the official World Champion Trophy from the 2022 Pokémon World Championships in London. I earned this trophy myself by taking 1st Place in Pokémon Unite the very first year the game was included in the World Championships. With Pokémon Unite’s end of service now… pic.twitter.com/ASgCB3yASu

The timing is tied to the game itself. His post links the sale to UNITE’s end of service, which is set for 23 March 2027 . We covered the shutdown and what it means for players in our report on the Pokémon UNITE shutdown date . Once the servers go dark, the list of UNITE world champions is closed for good, and the first trophy on that list becomes harder to replace. That scarcity is the case for a high price.

Before the listing went up, a thread on the r/PokeInvesting subreddit asked for advice on how to value and sell a World Championship trophy, using the same photos. It is not clear whether Junglebook posted it. According to Pokémon collector account PokeTCGAlerts, replies there suggested somewhere between $10,000 and $50,000. The same account called the $400,000 figure “the most ambitious Pokémon listing I’ve seen in a while”.

title: FC 27 TOTW 8 Predictions: Yamal, Raphinha and Mbappé
content:
LaLiga’s 11th round has given EA Sports FC 27 players plenty to think about before Team of the Week 8. Barcelona put six past Alavés, Real Madrid went 3-0 up at Racing de Santander on Sunday, and several Spanish players now have a strong case for an in-form card when EA reveals the next squad on Wednesday, 4 November.

Team of the Week cards arrive every Wednesday in Ultimate Team. TOTW 7 went live on 28 October with Kylian Mbappé at 92 as its headline card, alongside Gabriel at 90 and Klara Bühl at 89. These are the LaLiga players most likely to feature in TOTW 8, based on the results so far.

Barcelona’s 6-1 win over Alavés on Saturday is the obvious starting point. Raphinha scored twice , in the 8th and 41st minutes, and Lamine Yamal also scored twice, either side of half-time, and set up Fermín López for the second goal. López finished with a goal and two assists, both of them for Raphinha. Anthony Gordon added the sixth from a Rodri pass, before Mariano Díaz pulled one back for Alavés.

Yamal looks the strongest candidate of the three. Two goals and an assist in a 6-1 win is the kind of line EA usually rewards, and Raphinha’s brace gives him a similar claim. With only a handful of LaLiga places in each squad, López could miss out despite his three goal contributions.

Real Madrid’s trip to El Sardinero was Sunday’s late kick-off and was still being played as this article was prepared. Mbappé opened the scoring from the penalty spot early on, and Bellingham and Diomandé added goals as Madrid went 3-0 up.

Mbappé already has a TOTW 7 card, but EA can give a player in-forms in consecutive weeks, so he cannot be ruled out. Bellingham is the safer Madrid pick if EA wants a new name, with Diomandé an outside option depending on how the rest of the match goes.

title: 1win deny HOTU in Moscow and put 100 Thieves in pole
content:
HOTU were one series away from a sure Singapore Major place and now need Sunday night’s results in Buenos Aires to go their way.

1win won GLuck Moscow Cyber Games on Sunday with a 2-0 win over HOTU in the grand final, 13-9 on Anubis and 13-11 on Dust2. The title takes 1win to Stage 2 of the PGL Major Singapore, and it leaves HOTU without the invite a win would have guaranteed them.

As we wrote this morning , the Moscow final and FiReSPORTS Last Chance in Buenos Aires were the last two events that could move Europe’s final places before Valve’s VRS snapshot on 2 November. Moscow is settled. The last European invite now goes through Argentina, where 100 Thieves control their own fate and HOTU and Fnatic can only hope.

HOTU picked Anubis and held 6-6 at the half, but 1win took seven of the last ten rounds to close it out 13-9. Artem “ArtFr0st” Kharitonov, on loan from BetBoom, went 18-8 on the map. Dmitry “mizu” Kondratev did what he could on the other side with 21-13, 76.8 ADR and 90.9% KAST, the only HOTU player with more kills than deaths.

On 1win’s Dust2 pick, HOTU trailed 4-8 at the break and fought back to 11-11. The comeback stopped there: 1win won round 23 on a B execute and then the map, 13-11.

The lineup of Sergey “Ax1Le” Rykhtorov, Vladislav “nafany” Gorshkov, Andrey “BELCHONOKK” Yasinskiy, Petr “fame” Bolyshev and ArtFr0st only came together in August, and they are already 14th in HLTV’s world ranking.

title: RLCS : Geekay mise sur un roster français avec Seikoo, juicy et mtzr (off.)
content:
Le mercato Rocket League continue de redistribuer les cartes au sommet de la scène européenne. Après les annonces de Gentle Mates, Vitality et de la Karmine Corp, Geekay Esports a dévoilé son nouvel effectif pour les RLCS 2027, composé d’Enzo « Seikoo » Grondein, Charles « juicy » Sabiani et Mathis « mtzr » Hoareau. Deux recrues particulièrement expérimentées qui rejoignent l’un des jeunes talents prometteurs de la scène française. L’objectif est clair : construire un projet capable de rivaliser avec les meilleures formations européennes, malgré une concurrence qui s’annonce particulièrement relevée.

Juicy arrive en provenance de la Karmine Corp, avec laquelle il a notamment remporté le Paris Major en 2026, tandis que Seikoo quitte Manchester City. Les deux Français avaient rapidement décidé de s’associer durant cette intersaison et envisageaient initialement de jouer avec M0nkey M00n. Mais le double champion du monde a finalement choisi de rejoindre la reconstruction de la KC, laissant une place disponible dans le trio. Geekay a alors saisi l’occasion pour réunir les deux joueurs autour de mtzr, qui poursuit sa progression après deux saisons de développement au plus haut niveau.

Autre annonce importante, Andy « Kassio » Landais fait son retour sur le circuit RLCS. L’ancien joueur professionnel, passé par les staffs de BDS et Vitality, avait décidé de prendre sa retraite d’entraîneur en 2025. Après une expérience auprès de la sélection marocaine dans le cadre de la FIFAe World Cup 2026, finalement reportée, le Français de 25 ans a choisi de retrouver la compétition. Il explique notamment avoir renoué avec sa passion pour Rocket League, une motivation qui l’a convaincu d’accepter ce nouveau défi.

Malgré ce recrutement ambitieux, Geekay Esports devra passer par les qualifications ouvertes européennes pour espérer participer au Club Kick-Off de Londres, prévu en décembre. Contrairement à plusieurs de ses concurrents, la structure n’a pas été retenue parmi les organisations partenaires du RLCS Club Championship 2027. Le nouveau trio français fera toutefois ses premiers pas en compétition dès le 2 novembre à l’occasion de la Coupe de France Slash 2026, où il pourrait notamment croiser la route de Gentle Mates et de la Karmine Corp. Un premier test intéressant pour une équipe qui espère rapidement bousculer la hiérarchie européenne.

title: Gladiators Esports misses their PMGC 2026 dream by just 5 points
content:
Gladiators Esports have failed to qualify for PMGC 2026. India’s BMSD 2026 runners-up finished 4th at the BGMI International Cup (BMIC) 2026 in Mumbai on 144 points, after Dplus KIA’s Favian eliminated them in Match 18 on Miramar. Only the top two at BMIC earned PUBG Mobile Global Championship places, and Gladiators ended 7 points behind DRX in 2nd.

It is a hard way to go out. Gladiators won three Chicken Dinners at BMIC 2026, two of them on the final day, and walked into the last match just 3 points off a PMGC spot.

Gladiators needed a big final match and got 2 points. Going into Match 18, they sat 3rd on 142 points, 3 behind DRX (145) and 1 ahead of Dplus KIA (141). To take the runner-up slot, they had to outscore DRX by at least 4 points and Dplus KIA by at least 2.

Instead, Gladiators were knocked out early in the Miramar match by Favian’s Dplus KIA. They left with 2 points and finished on 144. DRX added 6 points to close on 151, and Dplus KIA were already on 145 and still alive when Gladiators went out. That pushed Gladiators down to 4th, with no way back into the top two.

The swing is the story, a single good finish still would have done it. Gladiators had scored 23 and 17 points in their two Day 3 Chicken Dinners, but the last game gave them almost nothing.

title: Vico Opens Up About Mental Health Struggles After Career-Best Fortnite Year
content:
BIG’s Taylor-Petrik “vic0” Gatschelhofer, known to most fans as Vico, has opened up about years of mental health struggles, five weeks after finishing third at the FNCS Global Championship and stepping away from competitive Fortnite. In posts on X on Sunday, he said he attempted to take his own life shortly before Globals, and that he no longer has contact with his family.

Vico’s 2026 run with Malibuca is why BIG called them “the best duo of all time” after Globals. They won the FNCS Major 1 Summit in Düsseldorf , then took the inaugural Fortnite Reload Elite Series at the Esports World Cup 2026.

Globals, at the Lotto Arena in Antwerp from 24 to 27 September, nearly made it three. The BIG pair led by 32 points going into the final game and finished third , four points behind champions SwizzY and Pixie, for $160,000 from the $2,000,000 prize pool. Our Globals grand finals report covers how that last game unfolded.

BIG’s chief gaming officer, Roman Reinhardt, summed up the result at the time: “Third place at Fortnite Globals. So close, but that’s part of it and it stings. Not everyone can say they were one kill away from the Globals win.” He added a line aimed at his players: “We believe in you 100%.” The club’s own post on X put it more simply: “No third trophy but still a great result.”

In October, BIG announced that Vico was one of ten finalists for Esports PC Player of the Year at the Esports Awards 2026, with the winners due to be revealed in Miami on 17 November. “Vico has had an incredible year, and his journey is truly special,” Reinhardt said then. Vico called the nomination “a huge honour”.

The first sign that something was wrong came on the final day of Globals. Vico said he had almost not attended the event, a comment picked up and shared by community accounts within hours. That evening he announced a break on X : “will be taking a break from competetive fortnite for a while. dealing with a lot of private stuff outside my competetive carreer and want to focus on that first and figure my life out. Will be back next year.”

title: NOVA Esports Earn VCT China 2027 Spot With 3-0 Final Win
content:

Unsettled Resentment never reached more than six rounds on a map: NOVA took Lotus 13-5, Abyss 13-5 and Split 13-6 .

It is a quick turnaround for a team that looked to be on the way out of the league. NOVA were one of four organisations reported to have been left off the 2027-28 partner list , alongside FunPlus Phoenix, Titan Esports Club and Wolves Esports. A week after losing one Threshold final, they won the other.

The Threshold ran over two weeks at THE HUB Performing Arts Center in Shanghai, from 21 October to 1 November, with each week’s winner taking a guest place in the 2027 league. Twelve teams entered, including former partners NOVA, FunPlus Phoenix, Titan, Wolves and Dragon Ranger Gaming.

NOVA’s first attempt came close. They beat Any Questions Gaming 2-1 in the Week 1 quarter-finals and KeepBest Gaming 2-0 in the semi-finals, then ran into Dragon Ranger Gaming in the grand final on 25 October. DRG won 3-0 , taking Summit 13-8, Split 13-3 and Lotus 13-9, and with it the first guest spot. DRG had swept their way there, beating Rare Atom 2-0, FunPlus Phoenix 2-1 and Titan 2-0 on the other side of the bracket. They had also been reported as missing out on partnership, so the win put them straight back into the league they were about to leave.

That left one place and a second week to fight for it. NOVA made the grand final again, and this time the opponent was Unsettled Resentment, who had beaten Octagonal Disposition Gaming 2-0 in Week 1 before going out to Titan 2-0 in the quarter-finals. The final itself was one-sided. NOVA held Unsettled Resentment to 16 rounds across three maps and closed the series without dropping a map.

The roster that won it is GuanG, swagzor, qiutiaN, Ezeir and cb. The players celebrated online soon after the final. For an organisation that was facing a year outside the top level, it means NOVA start 2027 in the league instead of outside it.

title: TYLOO Set to Miss Singapore Major After HyperX Retake Forfeit
content:
TYLOO were one best-of-three away from a strong position in the race for the PGL Major Singapore, and they never played it. The Chinese side forfeited their HyperX Retake Season 13 quarter-final against Metizport in Lisbon on 31 October so they could travel to IEM Beijing. That decision has all but handed the last Asian Major spot to Lynn Vision.

Before the quarter-final, HLTV’s invite prediction gave TYLOO a 68% chance of reaching Singapore. The forfeit cut that to 17%, and by the eve of the cutoff HLTV’s Asia tracker had TYLOO on 2.2% and Lynn Vision on 98.5%. Lynn Vision did not play a single match to get there. Invites come from the Valve Regional Standings (VRS) published on 2 November, so nothing is official until Valve’s numbers are out, but neither team has a match left that could change them.

Asia has five places at the Singapore Major. Four of them were settled before the weekend: The MongolZ, BC.Game, FlyQuest and Chinggis Warriors had all clinched. That left one spot and two Chinese teams chasing it, TYLOO and Lynn Vision.

TYLOO’s route ran through Lisbon. Season 13 is the last VRS LAN on the HyperX Retake circuit this year, and registration was open to any team willing to pay the €1,000 entry fee. TYLOO signed up, made it out of the groups and drew Metizport in the quarter-finals. A win there, and a deeper run after it, would have given them the ranking points to stay ahead of Lynn Vision when the standings froze.

That is why Lisbon carried so much weight. Neither TYLOO nor Lynn Vision had another match scheduled before the cutoff, so Lynn Vision’s total was already fixed. TYLOO’s was the only number in the race that could still move, and the Retake playoffs were the last place it could move upwards.

The match never took place. On 31 October the organisers announced that TYLOO and Natus Vincere (NAVI) had both pulled out: “NAVI & TYLOO have decided to forfeit their upcoming matches due to scheduling conflicts. As a result, their respective opponents will advance directly to the semifinals.” Metizport went through on a 1-0 forfeit, and NAVI’s playoff opponents, WhiteBIT Academy, advanced the same way. NAVI’s Major place never depended on a Retake result, so their withdrawal changes nothing for them.

title: GTA 6 Is Reportedly a 210GB Download, Boxed Copies Included
content:
Grand Theft Auto VI is going to need a lot of room. The standard edition is a 210GB download on PS5, according to PlayStation Game Size, an X account that tracks data from the PlayStation Store’s backend, and Insider Gaming says it can back the number up. Big games have passed 100GB for years. This one is harder to plan around, because the boxed version holds a download code instead of a disc, so every player faces the full GTA 6 download size.

The listing surfaced on 27 October and covers the $79.99 standard edition. It shows preloading from 12 November and a midnight release on 19 November, matching the dates Rockstar announced in June. It gives no size for the $99.99 Ultimate Edition or for Xbox Series X|S, and Rockstar hasn’t published a storage figure of its own so far.

The 210GB is also a download size rather than a final install size, and it doesn’t include a day-one patch. As Engadget pointed out , Insider Gaming warns that a patch could push the first-day download higher still.

Rockstar settled the disc question back in June. When pre-orders opened, its official announcement said the physical version would contain “a download code inside the box” and would go on sale on 12 November “to support pre-loading.” In practice the boxed copy is a voucher. Buying GTA 6 in a shop puts you in the same 210GB queue as buying it on the PlayStation Store, and the box mostly gives you something to put on a shelf. It does at least keep box buyers on the same schedule, since the code in the case works from the first day of preloading. On the Xbox Series S, which has no disc drive, a code was always the only option. We’ve gone through everything Rockstar has said about a GTA 6 disc version before, and nothing since has changed that picture.

Grand Theft Auto VI – 𝐃𝐨𝐰𝐧𝐥𝐨𝐚𝐝 𝐒𝐢𝐳𝐞 : 210 GB – 𝐒𝐭𝐚𝐧𝐝𝐚𝐫𝐝 ($79.99) Pre-Load : November 12 Release : November 19 𝐑𝐞𝐥𝐞𝐚𝐬𝐞 𝐓𝐢𝐦𝐞 : Midnight pic.twitter.com/5vXkgnqfC7

Part of the reason is arithmetic. A PS5 disc holds up to 100GB, so a game this size would have needed at least three of them, with a patch on top. Rockstar never gave its own reason for dropping the disc. VGC noted an earlier report that the decision was partly about preventing leaks before launch, and Take-Two has denied planning a disc release later.

title: Worlds 2026 : la Karmine Corp en quarts, BLG élimine HLE… le Swiss Stage a livré son verdict !
content:
L’enjeu était maximal pour les six dernières équipes encore en lice avec un bilan de 2-2 : une victoire pour rejoindre les playoffs, une défaite pour rentrer à la maison. Et la soirée a débuté par un duel franco-espagnol particulièrement attendu entre la Karmine Corp et Movistar KOI. Éliminée par l’équipe d’Ibai lors des LEC Summer Finals à Nice, la KC tenait sa revanche. Malgré une première manche très disputée, les hommes de Reapered ont fait la différence lors d’un teamfight autour du Dragon ancestral pour s’imposer après 40 minutes. La deuxième partie a tourné à la démonstration : victoire 18-4 en seulement 26 minutes, avec un Yike impérial sur Pantheon (9/0/5). Pour sa toute première participation aux Worlds, la Karmine Corp atteint déjà les quarts de finale, où elle retrouvera le champion du monde en titre, T1. Caliste devient au passage le cinquième Français à atteindre ce stade de la compétition, après YellOwStaR, sOAZ, Hans Sama et SkewMond. Canna retrouve quant à lui les quarts cinq ans après sa première qualification avec T1, tout en franchissant la barre des 100 éliminations aux Worlds.

C'ÉTAIT TELLEMENT TENDU, LET'S GOOOOOOO ! pic.twitter.com/27VxL3iaVd

Dans la deuxième rencontre, LOS a longtemps cru pouvoir prolonger son incroyable parcours, au lendemain de son élimination surprise de Team Liquid. Les Brésiliens ont même ouvert le score face à LYON, avant de voir Inspired et ses coéquipiers renverser la situation. La formation nord-américaine a d’abord égalisé au terme d’une manche particulièrement fermée de 47 minutes, conclue avec seulement neuf éliminations de chaque côté. LYON a ensuite pris le contrôle de la troisième partie, porté par un Inspired décisif sur Nocturne (2/0/10). Une victoire 2-1 synonyme de qualification pour les quarts, où Gen.G attend désormais les Nord-Américains pour un affrontement qui s’annonce particulièrement compliqué.

Enfin, le choc entre Bilibili Gaming et Hanwha Life Esports a offert l’une des plus belles manches de ce début de tournoi. Au terme de 41 minutes d’un niveau de jeu exceptionnel, BLG a pris l’avantage grâce à un Knight monstrueux sur Orianna (8/1/10). Le midlaner chinois a notamment fait basculer l’ultime teamfight avec une shockwave dévastatrice et un quadrakill. Il a remis ça lors de la deuxième manche, terminée avec un impressionnant 7/0/2 sur Locke (27 de KDA sur l’ensemble du BO3), pour offrir une victoire nette (2-0) à son équipe. BLG élimine ainsi Hanwha Life et prend sa revanche sur la finale du MSI, remportée par les Coréens.

LA SHOCKWAVE ! QUADRAKILL POUR KNIGHT pic.twitter.com/7pmcHATrHx

Le tableau des quarts de finale est désormais complet. La Karmine Corp affrontera T1 vendredi prochain, avec une éventuelle demi-finale contre le vainqueur de Dplus KIA – Bilibili Gaming. Dans l’autre partie de l’arbre, Gen.G retrouvera LYON, tandis que Top Esports et Invictus Gaming s’affronteront dans un duel 100 % chinois. Rendez-vous du 3 au 6 novembre à Allen, au Texas, pour quatre BO5 qui détermineront les derniers prétendants au titre mondial.

title: PGL Bucharest peaks at 667K viewers, short of Astana record
content:
FURIA against Nemiga was the most-watched series of PGL Masters Bucharest 2026, yet the event stays well short of PGL’s non-Major record.

FURIA ‘s 3-2 win over Nemiga Gaming on Saturday peaked at 667,736 concurrent viewers, according to Esports Charts . No other series in Bucharest came close: the next best was NAVI against Team Spirit in the group stage at 590,066.

Across 76 hours of airtime the event drew just over 20.1 million hours watched and an average audience of 264,558. Esports Charts still lists the tournament as being moderated, so the figures may move slightly. We covered the series itself in our grand final report .

The peak is more than double the April edition of PGL Bucharest, which FUT Esports won in front of a 320,700 peak , and well above the 518,849 that PGL Bucharest 2025 reached. Against the rest of the 2026 calendar, though, it sits in the lower half:

It is not PGL’s best non-Major peak either. That mark belongs to PGL Astana 2026, which Esports Charts lists as the organiser’s most popular non-Major Counter-Strike event at more than 1.16 million. PGL Cluj-Napoca in February, where Team Vitality against PARIVISION drew 908,945, also beat it by more than 240,000. Bucharest also finished below ESL Pro League Season 24, which peaked at 747,055 three weeks ago.

Two teams dominated the event’s five biggest series. FURIA played in three of them: the final, their group stage loss to Spirit (560,657) and the semi-final win over MOUZ (482,153). Spirit also featured three times, including against MOUZ (513,052), even though they went out before the playoffs.

title: d4v41, Jinggg bid farewell to Paper Rex
content:

title: Phantom Blade Zero Explodes on Steam, Peaking at 775K Players and Hitting #1 Top Seller
content:
Only a few days have passed since the global release of Phantom Blade Zero on October 29, and it continues to send shockwaves throughout the gaming community. The martial arts action RPG from S-Game has cemented its position as one of the biggest PC launches of the year, hitting a concurrent player peak of over 775,000 on Steam as per Steam Charts .

Phantom Blade Zero brings the speed and spectacle of kungfu cinema to life in an epic journey through the world of Kungfupunk. Get ready to draw your blade. Pre-load: Oct 27, 10 am Beijing Time / Oct 26, 7 pm PT Official game launch: Oct 29, 10 am Beijing Time / Oct 28, 7 pm PT… pic.twitter.com/FSHyhcjnse

It didn’t take long for the highly anticipated title to explode on the Steam charts, as it crossed the half-million mark within roughly ten hours of release, but the climb didn’t stop there. Within its first 24 hours, it had already hit a peak of more than 723,000 concurrent players. A couple of days later, it has managed to push past a whopping 775,000 active players , putting it among the most-played games to appear on the platform this year.

With this milestone, Phantom Blade Zero became Steam’s most-played single-player title of 2026, overtaking Resident Evil Requiem , which had hit a peak of 344,214 players.

As a result of its huge surge in popularity, Phantom Blade Zero is also dominating the sales charts. It currently sits at #1 on Steam’s Top Sellers list, and it had secured the spot ahead of launch, surpassing juggernauts like Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 .

The game’s reception has also been pretty warm within the community. It is currently sitting at a Very Positive rating on Steam, and while some complaints have surfaced here and there, the majority of gamers seem to be enjoying it. Word of mouth tends to matter most for demanding action games, and the early response suggests players are sticking around.

title: PGL set Schengen event for September 2027 without open qualifier
content:
All 22 places at PGL’s fifth tier one event of 2027 go out as VRS invites, and a missed visa deadline counts as a withdrawal.

PGL has revealed the structure of PGL CS2 #5, a 16-team LAN in the Schengen area from 2 to 12 September 2027, with $1,000,000 in winnings and a further $300,000 in VRS bonuses. The organiser published the details on its news site and on X on Saturday afternoon, while the PGL Masters Bucharest 2026 grand final was being played. No city or venue has been named.

PGL has confirmed the full structure for its 5th Tier 1 Counter-Strike 2 tournament of 2027, to be held in the Schengen area between September 2 and 12, 2027. The tournament will feature a total of $1,300,000 in rewards, including $1,000,000 in prize winnings and $300,000 in VRS… pic.twitter.com/aQ9ZOlNq4Q

Every team gets there through the Valve Regional Standings. Fourteen teams are invited directly from the Global VRS, starting from No. 1, and the last two places go to the winners of an eight-team EU Closed Qualifier, played online on Fragnet Arena from 24 to 27 May 2027. The eight qualifier teams are also invited, from the Europe VRS, beginning with the highest-ranked European side that has not already been invited to the main event. That makes 22 direct invites in total, with no wildcards and, unlike PGL Bucharest 2027 and the April event in China, no open qualifier.

The comparison with PGL’s April event in China is clear. That tournament has open qualifiers in Europe and Asia and a separate Asian path to the main event. In September, a team outside the global top 14 can only get in through the European closed qualifier, and only if it is high enough in the Europe VRS to be invited to it.

Invites four months before the event also mean rosters are locked in early. A team can only accept if at least three of its players were on the invited roster on 3 May and play every match of the tournament. PGL’s post does not describe the main event bracket. When PGL unveiled its 2027 and 2028 plans in March, it said its events would keep a format close to the Majors, with Bo3 Swiss stages and eight-team playoffs, Dust2.us reported.

title: Marvel Rivals Night of Illusions Chapter 1 solution: Nursepool’s Infirmary
content:

The first thing you need to do is find the Red Vial on the hospital trolley located to the left of the screen. Select it and give it to Nursepool. This resets the chapter, but that’s supposed to happen.

title: FURIA Comeback Against Nemiga to Win PGL Masters Bucharest
content:
FURIA are the winners of the PGL Masters Bucharest 2026, beating Nemiga 3-2. Having lost the opening map, the Brazilians were tested until the final map of the game by upstarts from CIS, as all five maps were needed to crown the champion in Romania.

This win marks their second tier-1 trophy of the second half of the season, following their Thunderpick World Championship title in October. FURIA, as a team, fell short multiple times in the first half of the season, despite making deep runs at a number of events; however, they managed to secure important victories against the likes of MOUZ and BetBoom, but NAVI and Spirit exposed the cracks earlier in the event.

CAMPEÕES DA #PGLBUCHAREST ! #FURIACS pic.twitter.com/egorYAOZhZ

Nemiga came in with hot hands to kick off the Grand Finals, securing a whopping 10-2 half on the T side of Ancient. With a solid start to the series, they secured a flawless second half to close out the map and take an early lead in the series. FURIA returned the favor in the following map as they levelled the series with a 13-5 win in Dust2. With a level scoreline, FURIA went on to secure yet another one-sided map, taking the lead with a 13-2 win in Cache, putting Nemiga on series point.

Nemiga found their footing in the 4th map as they kept FURIA on the back foot for the better part of the map, as a tight scoreline sent the series to the final map of the series. Starting on the defensive side of Nuke, FURIA edged out a narrow lead before maintaining their momentum on the offensive side, having switched sides. Winning the pistol helped extend the lead further as FURIA pushed the series over the line with a 13-6 scoreline. YEKINDAR’s 82 kills across five maps proved instrumental in the side’s dominance at the tournament as the Latvian secured a whopping 1.56 IR.

FURIA have secured an important victory that will help build their confidence ahead of the highly anticipated PGL Major . The losses to NAVI and Spirit have raised questions, especially given the little time they have left. On the other hand, a convincing win over MOUZ has shown everyone that when it comes to playoffs, they are capable of hanging with the best teams, but only time will tell if they can achieve similar results against the likes of Vitality and Falcons.

title: Heretics a déjà bouclé son roster LEC
content:
Team Heretics n’a pas perdu de temps sur le marché des transferts. Alors que les Worlds 2026 ne sont pas encore terminés, la structure espagnole aurait déjà finalisé son cinq de départ pour la prochaine saison de LEC, à en croire les informations de Sheep Esports . Un recrutement particulièrement rapide après une année à oublier, marquée par une dixième place au Spring Split et une neuvième au Summer Split. Malgré plusieurs changements de joueurs et l’arrivée d’Erlend « Nukeduck » Holm au poste d’entraîneur, Heretics n’avait jamais réussi à trouver la bonne formule.

Pour 2027, trois nouveaux visages devraient rejoindre l’effectif : Razork, Jackies et Jun. En fin de contrat avec Fnatic, Iván « Razork » Martín aurait choisi de rejoindre Heretics malgré l’intérêt de GIANTX, offrant à l’organisation espagnole un jungler expérimenté et reconnu sur la scène européenne. Sur la midlane, Adam « Jackies » Jeřábek remplacerait Serin après son départ de GIANTX, tandis que Yoon « Jun » Se-jun, également passé par la structure espagnole, prendrait la place de Way au poste de support. Trois recrutements qui témoignent de la volonté de Heretics de retrouver rapidement de la compétitivité.

Ces arrivées devraient compléter un effectif construit autour de Sebastian « Tracyn » Wojtoń et Byeon « Hype » Jeong-hyeon, les deux seuls joueurs conservés de la saison précédente. Le toplaner polonais a prolongé son contrat jusqu’en 2028, tandis que l’ADC coréen aurait accepté une réduction de salaire pour poursuivre l’aventure. Un effort financier qui aurait notamment facilité la reconstruction du roster. De son côté, Nukeduck disposerait désormais des pleins pouvoirs sportifs pour mener ce nouveau projet et tenter d’installer une véritable stabilité dans l’équipe.

Avec cette composition, Heretics espère enfin franchir un cap après plusieurs saisons décevantes. Depuis son arrivée en LEC en 2023, la structure n’a jamais fait mieux qu’une quatrième place lors du Summer Split de sa première année. La stabilité reste d’ailleurs un véritable défi : avec ces trois recrues, pas moins de 25 joueurs auront porté le maillot de l’équipe première depuis ses débuts dans l’élite européenne. Reste à savoir si ce nouveau cinq, qui mêle expérience et jeunes talents, permettra à Heretics de s’imposer durablement parmi les prétendants aux playoffs en 2027.

La KCB privilégierait de son côté la continuité de son projet de formation, tout en conservant un élément expérimenté pour accompagner ses jeunes recrues. Reste à savoir si cette nouvelle génération saura rapidement s’adapter aux exigences de la LFL. Après une saison 2026 loin de ses standards habituels, la Karmine Corp Blue espère retrouver les premiers rôles en 2027, avec un effectif largement renouvelé mais toujours profondément lié au Blue Wall.

title: eeiu reportedly heading back to NRG after FURIA exit
content:
The Canadian initiator, benched by FURIA in July, has a verbal agreement to return to the club where his career took off.

Daniel “eeiu” Vucenovic has reached a verbal agreement to join NRG for the 2027 VCT Americas season, Sheep Esports reports . According to the outlet’s sources, Cloud9 were also interested in the initiator, and NRG are extending head coach Malkolm “bonkar” Rench’s contract at the same time. Neither NRG nor eeiu have commented, and nothing is official.

It would be a homecoming. eeiu played for NRG from October 2020 to 2022, before the partnership league started in 2023.

eeiu started in competitive Valorant with T1 Academy in the summer of 2020 before moving to NRG that October. When NRG built a new roster for the partnership league, he joined M80 in December 2022, and the 2023 season was his breakout: M80 won the North America Challengers Split 1, the Mid-Season Face Off and the Challengers Playoffs, then lost the VCT Ascension Americas final 1-3 to The Guard.

That earned him a move to 100 Thieves in November 2023. In his first partnered season, 100 Thieves swept G2 3-0 to win VCT Americas Stage 1 2024 and finished fourth at Masters Shanghai. He was also named VCT Americas Initiator of the Year in 2024. 2025 was a weaker year for the team, and 100 Thieves let him go on 31 October 2025.

At FURIA, eeiu won VCT Americas Kickoff 2026, beating MIBR 3-2 in the final. FURIA then went out 1-2 to BBL Esports in seventh to eighth place at Masters Santiago, but eeiu was the team’s best player there by some distance.

title: VCT EMEA : Gentle Mates au complet avec Boaster
content:
Le mercato VALORANT réserve décidément son lot de surprises. Selon les informations de Sheep Esports , Jake « Boaster » Howlett aurait trouvé un accord verbal avec Gentle Mates pour la saison 2027. Une nouvelle particulièrement marquante, tant le Britannique est devenu indissociable de Fnatic depuis son arrivée en 2021. Capitaine emblématique de la structure, il a accompagné son ascension parmi les meilleures équipes mondiales, remportant notamment le LOCK//IN de São Paulo et le Masters de Tokyo en 2023. Son départ marquerait ainsi la fin d’une époque pour Fnatic, qui préparerait également une profonde reconstruction avec l’arrivée attendue de valyn à la tête de son effectif.

Chez Gentle Mates, Boaster devrait retrouver Emir « Alfajer » Beder, son ancien coéquipier chez Fnatic, lui aussi annoncé en partance vers la structure française. Les deux hommes seraient accompagnés de Denis-Stefan « kozzy » Aionitoaei, Martin « MAGNUM » Penkov et Uğur « Ruxic » Güç, tous déjà évoqués par Sheep Esports ces dernières semaines. L’Américain Adam « kaplan » Kaplan devrait également rejoindre le projet au sein du staff technique. Sur le papier, cette association entre l’expérience de Boaster, le talent d’Alfajer et plusieurs joueurs prometteurs pourrait donner naissance à l’un des effectifs les plus attendus du VCT EMEA 2027.

Cette révolution intervient après une année 2026 particulièrement contrastée pour les deux organisations. Fnatic a connu une saison très compliquée, manquant notamment le Masters de Santiago, l’Esports World Cup et les Champions de Shanghai. Les résultats individuels de Boaster ont également suscité des interrogations, particulièrement lors du Stage 2, où le Britannique figurait parmi les joueurs les moins performants du championnat sur plusieurs statistiques. Un changement d’environnement pourrait donc lui permettre de relancer sa carrière après six années riches en succès.

De son côté, Gentle Mates cherche à retrouver la dynamique de son excellent début de saison 2026. Deuxième du Kickoff EMEA et qualifié pour le Masters de Santiago, le club français avait ensuite progressivement perdu pied, jusqu’à une élimination dès les Play-Ins du Stage 2 face à des formations issues du Tier 2. Avec le départ attendu de marteen vers Fnatic et une reconstruction presque totale de son cinq de départ, M8 semble désormais prêt à miser sur un projet beaucoup plus ambitieux. Si les accords rapportés se concrétisent, les retrouvailles entre Boaster et Alfajer pourraient bien devenir l’un des grands événements du mercato européen.

title: LAR rifle files disappear from CS2 two days after leaking
content:
A silent Counter-Strike 2 update on Friday night removed the lever-action rifle that dataminers found on Wednesday, along with the folder marked “do_not_ship”.

Valve pushed an update to Counter-Strike 2 at Friday 23:14 CET without patch notes, and the files for the unreleased LAR rifle went with it. SteamDB’s file list for the build shows 30 files removed, all of them tied to the weapon.

The LAR first turned up in Wednesday’s update, the one that brought the silent reload toggle and the Big Head mutator. We covered it then : dataminers described it as a renamed version of the earlier leaked M14, a Winchester-style rifle that reloads one bullet at a time, with its materials stored in a folder called “do_not_ship”.

The removed files cover every part of the weapon that had shipped to players’ clients:

The same build made small changes to the game’s language files and to the music kit sound files. Valve have not commented on the LAR, and nothing in the update says whether the rifle is cancelled or simply pulled back into internal testing.

The folder name already suggested that the LAR was never meant to reach players with Wednesday’s update, and Friday’s build takes it back out. The silent reload animations among the removed files show that the rifle was built with the new reload system in mind.

title: MOUZ sweep Vitality to take bronze and keep VRS top spot
content:
Third place in Bucharest came with something bigger for MOUZ: the number one spot in the VRS, two days before the Major invitations.

MOUZ finished third at PGL Masters Bucharest 2026 after a 2-0 win over Team Vitality on Saturday morning, 13-7 on their own Nuke pick and 13-7 on Vitality’s Inferno. The result keeps them first in the Valve Regional Standings, and the gap to Vitality grows from two points to 40.

The bronze match doubled as a straight fight for the top of the VRS. MOUZ came in on 1,949 points and Vitality on 1,947, and on HLTV’s VRS calculator the win adds seven points for MOUZ while Vitality lose 31. A Vitality win would have put them back on top. Instead MOUZ hold the spot with 1,956 points as Valve’s 2 November cut-off for the Singapore Major invitations approaches. Both teams were always going to be invited; the question was who would sit first.

May not be the final, but doesnt mean you can't end with a statement. pic.twitter.com/zJF4UU9AAW

Before the match, the analysts on PGL’s desk agreed that MOUZ had more to play for. Vitality were without apEX, who is at home on paternity leave, and had lost 2-0 to Nemiga in Friday’s semi-final. MOUZ, a rebuilt side with PR and xelex brought in from the academy, had the chance to call themselves the best team in the world on Valve’s list. For Vitality, Pimp said, the top spot “doesn’t really mean anything”.

There was also a score to settle. Vitality beat MOUZ 3-0 in the ESL Pro League Season 24 final on 11 October, and MOUZ had won only three of their last ten maps against them before today.

title: Eternal Fire come back from 0-2 to beat fnatic in Barcelona
content:
The Turkish side won Stake Ranked Episode 5 through the lower bracket, and the trophy leaves fnatic’s Major hopes hanging on other teams’ results this weekend.

Eternal Fire are Stake Ranked Episode 5 champions after a reverse sweep of fnatic in Friday’s best-of-five grand final in Barcelona. fnatic took Anubis 13-8 and Ancient 13-2, then lost Cache, Dust II and Mirage as Eternal Fire turned the series around to win 3-2.

According to HLTV’s records, it is only the 14th time a team has come back from 0-2 in a Bo5 grand final on LAN.

fnatic had been the cleanest team in the event until the final. They swept Astralis, BIG and MIBR on their way through the upper bracket and won the first two maps of the final as well, ten maps in a row in Barcelona. The Ancient map was the most one-sided of the whole series: Eternal Fire won two rounds.

Eternal Fire took the long way. They reached the final from the lower bracket, beating Astralis 2-1 in the lower semi-final and MIBR 2-0 in the lower final earlier on Friday, so the grand final was their second series of the day.

title: molodoy says eye operation has eased his mind before Bucharest final
content:
FURIA’s AWPer told PGL’s broadcast that a minor operation before the event stopped him overthinking his eyes, and that Saturday’s grand final means facing two friends.

Danil “ molodoy ” Golubenko believes a minor eye operation before PGL Masters Bucharest is part of the reason his form has returned. The 21-year-old spoke to James Banks on PGL’s broadcast after FURIA beat MOUZ 2-1 in Friday’s semi-final, a series in which he went +15 on Dust2 .

Banks noted that the two had spoken at several events since molodoy’s problems with his eyes began, and asked where he is now. molodoy said:

I think it’s helped for me. And I think it’s more helps in mind. And you’re not focusing about this. And you’re not overthinking about your eyes.

He added that FURIA are “just improving this tournament” and “confident now”, after a 2026 in which the team knew they had problems.

molodoy also explained the moment Banks picked out from the team’s comms. FURIA trailed 4-2 on their Dust2 pick when YEKINDAR told the team to communicate better, and they won 11 of the next 13 rounds. molodoy said the rest of the team had left YEKINDAR alone when he went out long: “We don’t say anything for him to out. We don’t say we have flash, and we’re just bad, bro.”

title: Unreal Engine Vulnerability Puts Modded Games at Risk
content:
Unreal Engine ships with a default setting that can let community-made content open and run files on a player’s Windows PC, according to a vulnerability record published on 14 October. The researcher who found it says Epic Games has sent only an automatic reply since he reported it in July, and the hotfix Epic released a week after the disclosure doesn’t mention it.

The flaw, CVE-2026-14765 , is in LaunchURL, a Blueprint node that games use to open web links. Unreal checks those links against a filter, but the filter’s list of allowed link types is empty by default, and an empty list lets everything through. That includes links that point to files on the player’s own machine. The record covers Unreal Engine versions up to and including 5.8.0, rates the issue 7.7 out of 10, or High, and classes it as an insecure default (CWE-1188).

Any Unreal game that loads Blueprints made by its players, such as custom maps or mods, may be affected. Games that don’t load player-made Blueprints aren’t.

The advisory from AHA!, the Austin, Texas hacker group that assigned the CVE, explains the chain. On Windows, LaunchURL hands any link that isn’t http or https to the operating system’s “open” command. If the link points to a file, Windows opens it the way it would if you double-clicked it, and for file types such as .exe, .bat, .cmd, .vbs, .msi and .lnk, opening means running.

A malicious map or mod therefore only needs to save a file somewhere on the PC and then point LaunchURL at it. AHA! says the official score understates the risk for games built around user content. The score assumes the attacker needs local access and the player has to do something, but in a game with a Workshop the player’s only action is loading a map.

Khael Kugler, a lead security engineer at Praetorian, traced the problem to the engine while looking at MECCHA CHAMELEON, a $5.99 hide-and-seek game built in Unreal Engine 5 that came out on Steam in June. It was a surprise hit. SteamDB recorded a peak of 340,534 players on 21 June, and the developer said it had sold 20 million copies in just over two months, Game Developer reported . Players share custom maps through the Steam Workshop.

title: NIP Group Raises Its Share Limit to 10 Billion as It Pays for Bitcoin Miners in Stock
content:
NIP Group, the Nasdaq-listed company that owns Ninjas in Pyjamas, has raised the number of shares it is allowed to issue fivefold, from 2 billion to 10 billion. Shareholders approved the change at an extraordinary general meeting in Hong Kong on 16 October, according to a filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission. The filing doesn’t give the vote counts.

It is the second big increase in 15 months. At a meeting in July 2025, shareholders had already raised the limit from 500 million shares to 2 billion. Over that period, NIP has been paying for Bitcoin mining machines with new stock.

Four days after the vote, NIP disclosed its third deal to buy mining machines with its own stock. Under the purchase agreement , dated 24 September and filed on 20 October, the sellers receive up to 247,091,740 Class A shares for machines with about 4.47 exahashes per second (EH/s) of computing power. At the agreed rate of $6.12 per terahash, the deal is worth about $27.35 million.

The agreement says NIP had 431,520,600 Class A shares outstanding when it was signed, so the new shares would add about 57% to that count. NIP also has two classes of B shares, and the filings don’t give a current total across all classes. Under the new limit, NIP can issue up to 8.78 billion Class A shares, up from 1.76 billion. Either side can walk away if the deal hasn’t closed by 31 October. Co-chief executive Hicham Chahine told Decrypt this week that the batch has closed, but no filing confirming that had appeared by 30 October.

The first two batches followed the same pattern. In June 2025 NIP agreed to buy about 3.11 EH/s of machines for about 119.6 million Class A shares, and said they would mine about 60 Bitcoin a month. They produced about 151 Bitcoin from September to November 2025, roughly 50 a month. A second, larger deal in November 2025, for about 8.19 EH/s and up to 314.5 million shares, has been closing in stages, and NIP’s latest filing on it said one closing remained.

NIP says the three purchases take its fleet to about 13.85 EH/s, which it expects to produce about 195 Bitcoin a month at full deployment. Chahine said that “scaling our hashrate to nearly 14 EH/s solidifies our position as a significant player in the Bitcoin mining space”.

title: RLCS : Vitality frappe fort avec nass, Oski et diaz (off.)
content:
C’est une nouvelle ère qui s’ouvre chez Team Vitality. Après une saison 2026 marquée par plusieurs belles performances, mais aussi de nombreuses désillusions, la Ruche a choisi de renouveler intégralement son effectif Rocket League. Le départ d’Alexis « zen » Bernier vers Gentle Mates, où il évoluera aux côtés de Vatira et Atow, avait lancé les grandes manœuvres. Brice « ExoTiiK » Bigeard et Gaspar « stizzy » Rosalén ont également quitté l’organisation, mettant un terme à une aventure qui n’aura pas permis à Vitality de retrouver les sommets mondiaux.

Pour leur succéder, Vitality a officialisé les arrivées de Nassim « nass » Bali, Oskar « Oski » Gozdowski et du Brésilien diaz. Les deux premiers débarquent directement de Gentle Mates, effectuant ainsi le chemin inverse de zen, tandis que diaz arrive en provenance de Spacestation Gaming. Un recrutement ambitieux qui permet à la structure française de réunir trois joueurs au profil offensif, capables de rivaliser avec les meilleures équipes du circuit. Benjamin « Eversax » Wagner, lui, conserve son poste d’entraîneur et sera chargé de trouver rapidement les automatismes nécessaires à ce nouveau trio.

Cette reconstruction intervient après un exercice 2026 contrasté. Vitality avait pourtant atteint la finale du Boston Major, finalement perdue face à Gentle Mates (2-4), avant de remporter deux tournois régionaux européens. Mais les performances irrégulières et les éliminations répétées face aux principaux concurrents ont progressivement fragilisé le projet. Au Paris Major, la Ruche avait notamment échoué aux portes de la finale après une défaite particulièrement serrée contre la Karmine Corp (3-4).

Avec nass, Oski et diaz, Vitality espère désormais retrouver une place parmi les références internationales de Rocket League. Ce mercato redistribue également les cartes au sommet de la scène européenne, alors que Gentle Mates a constitué un trio particulièrement impressionnant autour de zen, Vatira et Atow. Les premiers tournois régionaux des RLCS 2027 permettront de mesurer le potentiel de cette nouvelle formation, avec un objectif évident pour la Ruche : transformer ce grand remaniement en titres majeurs.

title: Gentle Mates GC come from a map down to beat Shopify Rebellion Gold and reach Game Changers final
content:
Gentle Mates GC, on their Championship debut, beat Shopify Rebellion Gold 2-1 in the upper bracket final in São Paulo. The French-based side go into Sunday's best-of-five grand final with a two-map ban advantage, while Shopify Rebellion Gold must come through the lower final.

Gentle Mates GC are into the grand final of the VCT Game Changers Championship 2026. They beat Shopify Rebellion Gold 2-1 in the upper bracket final in São Paulo on Friday 30 October. The French-based side dropped the opening map and then took the next two. Both teams had arrived at the match with every map at the event won.

Shopify Rebellion Gold won map one, which lasted 53 minutes. On the second map they fought back to 10-10, but Gentle Mates closed it out 13-11 after 55 minutes. The decider on Summit ran for 57 minutes and finished 13-10 to Gentle Mates.

Coming through the upper bracket gives Gentle Mates a two-map ban advantage in the grand final. Shopify Rebellion Gold, led at the event by interim in-game leader alexis, drop into the lower bracket final against KRÜ Blaze.

This is Gentle Mates’ first appearance at the Championship. Their line-up of Marti, Nami, Wens, tokameite and berryx reached the upper final with 2-0 wins over Team Liquid Brazil and MIBR GC. Their last three EMEA Stage 3 results before the event were wins over G2 Gozen and SK Nebula, both 2-1, and a 3-2 defeat to G2 Gozen.

The Elo power rankings already had Gentle Mates ahead. They sit fourth with a rating of 1844 and a 33-7 record from 40 rated matches. Shopify Rebellion Gold are sixth on 1809, with a 40-20 record from 60 rated matches.

title: Worlds 2026 : coup de tonnerre, G2 et Team Liquid éliminés…
content:
La première surprise de la soirée est venue du duel des Amériques entre Team Liquid et LOS. Pourtant favori après son exploit contre Anyone’s Legend au tour précédent, le champion des LCS a complètement manqué son rendez-vous. Les Brésiliens ont frappé les premiers grâce à une redoutable botlane Ashe-Séraphine et un Curse impérial sur Trundle (7/0/6). Liquid a ensuite arraché l’égalisation au terme d’une deuxième manche de 38 minutes, en s’appuyant sur une composition particulièrement efficace en teamfights.

Mais le scénario a tourné au cauchemar pour les Nord-Américains dans la manche décisive. Au terme d’une bataille de 47 minutes, marquée par plusieurs occasions manquées de conclure, LOS a finalement trouvé l’ouverture dans la base adverse. Grand artisan de cette victoire, ZEST a terminé avec un impressionnant 10/1/3 sur Tristana, permettant aux Brésiliens de s’imposer 2-1. LOS poursuit donc son aventure avec un bilan de 2-2 dans le Swiss Stage, tandis que Team Liquid quitte la compétition devant son public, malgré les promesses entrevues lors de sa victoire contre le champion de LPL.

Dans l’autre rencontre de la soirée, le choc entre G2 Esports et Hanwha Life Esports a rapidement tourné à la démonstration coréenne. Les Samouraïs n’ont jamais réussi à trouver la solution face au champion du MSI, qui a imposé son rythme dès la première manche. Kanavi a notamment livré une prestation remarquable sur Lee Sin, terminant avec un score de 8/2/10 pour offrir un premier point convaincant à son équipe.

Malgré un début de deuxième partie encourageant de BrokenBlade sur Camille, G2 a rapidement été dépassé. Gumayusi a fait des ravages avec son Lucian (10/1/3), parfaitement accompagné par le Swain de Zeka (2/0/7), véritable mur infranchissable pour les Européens. Hanwha Life a conclu cette dernière manche en seulement 26 minutes, scellant une victoire expéditive 2-0 et mettant fin au parcours de G2. HLE jouera désormais sa qualification en quarts de finale face à Bilibili Gaming, dans le choc du cinquième round du Swiss Stage. Les deux autres affiches opposeront la Karmine Corp à Movistar KOI, garantissant à l’Europe au moins un représentant dans le Top 8 mondial, et LOS à LYON. Trois BO3 décisifs, programmés ce samedi à partir de 18h (heure française).

title: KC vs KOI pour une place en playoffs des Worlds 2026
content:
Le destin a réservé un scénario particulièrement intéressant aux représentants européens. Après avoir éliminé CTBC Flying Oyster (2-0) pour revenir à 2-2 dans le Swiss Stage, la Karmine Corp retrouvera Movistar KOI dès 18h dans un BO3 décisif pour la qualification en quarts de finale. Un tirage qui devrait ravir Caliste, lequel avait justement désigné la formation espagnole comme son adversaire préféré pour cette dernière rencontre. De son côté, KOI devra rebondir après sa lourde défaite face à T1 (0-2) lors du quatrième round.

L’enjeu est immense pour les deux formations. Avec l’élimination de G2 Esports face à Hanwha Life (0-2), l’Europe a perdu l’un de ses principaux favoris, mais elle est désormais assurée de compter au moins un représentant dans le Top 8 mondial. Pour la KC, ce serait une nouvelle étape majeure dans son parcours international, tandis que KOI espère confirmer sa place parmi les meilleures équipes de la compétition. Une chose est certaine : au terme de ce duel fratricide, une équipe européenne poursuivra son aventure, tandis que l’autre devra faire ses valises.

Mais l’affiche la plus prestigieuse de ce dernier round opposera Hanwha Life Esports à Bilibili Gaming aux alentours de minuit. Les Coréens arrivent lancés après leur démonstration face à G2, portée notamment par les excellentes prestations de Kanavi et Gumayusi. En face, BLG se retrouve dos au mur après sa défaite contre Top Esports (1-2). Deux formations annoncées parmi les grandes prétendantes au titre mondial se disputeront donc un unique billet pour les quarts de finale, avec une élimination particulièrement douloureuse pour le perdant.

Enfin, LOS et LYON compléteront le programme de ce cinquième round, dans une confrontation entre deux équipes qui ont déjà déjoué plusieurs pronostics. Les Brésiliens viennent notamment de créer la surprise en éliminant Team Liquid (2-1), première tête de série nord-américaine, tandis que LYON tentera de prolonger son aventure après sa défaite contre Invictus Gaming. Les trois rencontres se disputeront ce samedi en BO3, avec une qualification en quarts de finale pour les vainqueurs et une élimination définitive pour les perdants.

title: Overwatch players get New Evolution Doomfist skin for free
content:
Overwatch players can now unlock a brand-new Doomfist skin for free. Here’s how to get it yourself and what the New Evolution Doomfist skin means in the story and lore.

title: « La LCK le dit elle-même » : la Karmine Corp fait parler jusqu’en Corée
content:
Dos au mur après deux défaites frustrantes contre LYON et Bilibili Gaming, la Karmine Corp a parfaitement réagi face à CTBC Flying Oyster. Un succès précieux, marqué par une deuxième manche particulièrement compliquée, mais qui permet aux Français de revenir à 2-2 dans le Swiss Stage. Interrogé par nos confrères de DPM Esports , Caliste a reconnu les difficultés rencontrées sur la botlane, tout en saluant la réaction collective de son équipe. « Ce genre de partie peut arriver, et réussir à renverser la situation montre beaucoup de bonnes choses sur un groupe. » Une victoire qui redonne confiance à la KC avant son ultime BO3, décisif pour une qualification en quarts de finale.

Mais le jeune ADC français voit surtout beaucoup plus loin. Malgré les deux revers concédés dans ce Swiss Stage, Caliste estime que la Karmine Corp possède les armes pour rivaliser avec les meilleures formations du monde. Et les retours des équipes coréennes à l’entraînement semblent lui donner raison. « Nous savons que nous pouvons aller très, très loin. Je pense que ce sont les équipes de LCK qui le disent elles-mêmes. Nous pouvons être une équipe vraiment dangereuse » , assure-t-il. Selon lui, la KC affiche en scrims un visage particulièrement agressif, avec une excellente phase de lane et une capacité à prendre des risques qui surprendrait plusieurs adversaires asiatiques. Reste désormais à reproduire ce niveau sur scène, où la pression et les erreurs d’exécution ont parfois coûté très cher aux Français.

Un optimisme également partagé par Canna, particulièrement confiant après la victoire contre CFO. Dans une interview accordée au média sud-coréen Inven Global , le toplaner estime que son équipe a encore progressé ces derniers jours. « Notre niveau en scrims s’est encore amélioré récemment. L’équipe a trouvé un très bon équilibre. Même si nous comptons actuellement deux défaites, ce sont des matchs que nous aurions largement pu remporter. » Le Coréen pointe notamment les erreurs commises lors de certains combats d’équipe, mais refuse de voir une limite au potentiel de la KC : « Si nous soignons un peu notre exécution, je pense qu’il n’y a aucune équipe que nous ne pouvons pas battre. »

Pour franchir cette dernière marche, la Karmine Corp entend notamment simplifier ses drafts et privilégier des conditions de victoire plus claires, comme l’explique Caliste. Le Français ne cache pas non plus sa préférence pour Movistar KOI lors du tirage au sort, qu’il considère comme l’adversaire le plus abordable parmi les équipes encore en course. Canna, de son côté, préférerait éviter une formation de LCK avant les quarts de finale. Mais quel que soit l’adversaire, le message est clair : la KC croit toujours en ses chances de réaliser un grand parcours aux Worlds 2026, et compte bien prouver sur scène que les performances remarquées à l’entraînement ne doivent rien au hasard.

title: Discord’s IPO Has Stalled As Investors Can’t Agree What It’s Worth
content:
Discord filed confidentially for a US IPO in January, and people familiar with the plan told Bloomberg it was aiming to debut in March, TechCrunch reported . Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan were hired to run the offering. Ten months after the filing, the chat app is still private, and its paperwork still hasn’t been made public.

The stalled Discord IPO has left its investors to put their own prices on the company, and their numbers are far apart. Fund reports filed with the SEC in recent weeks, along with prices from the secondary market where early shareholders sell to new buyers, value a Discord share at anywhere from $23.51 to $36.79. Every one of those figures is below the $55.06 a share Discord charged in 2021, when a $500 million round valued it at about $15 billion.

A listing can’t happen quickly from here. Under SEC rules, a company that files in private has to make its registration statement public at least 15 days before it starts pitching the shares to investors. Discord hadn’t done that by 30 October, so an IPO is weeks away at the earliest, and no new date has been reported. Discord hasn’t said why the March target slipped.

Fidelity has the lowest number. Its Growth Company Fund holds 70,000 Discord Series I preferred shares, bought in September 2021 for $3.85 million, and valued them at $1.65 million on 31 August, its quarterly holdings report shows . That works out to $23.51 a share, 57% below what Fidelity paid, and other Fidelity funds that own the shares use the same price. The low mark isn’t new. Fidelity’s funds already valued the stake at less than half its cost in August 2023, and the latest figure is a little higher than the $22.28 they used in the spring.

ARK Venture Fund is close behind. Its annual report for the year to 31 July values its 176,670 Discord common shares at $4.68 million, or about $26.51 each, according to the filing . ARK bought them in November 2022 for $4.37 million, so its holding sits about 7% above cost.

The secondary market is more generous. Forge , which tracks trades in private company shares, put Discord’s indicative price at $36.79 on 30 October, up 17% in six months, and values the company at $10.02 billion at that price. That is 56% above Fidelity’s mark and about a third below the 2021 round.

title: Forza Creator Dan Greenawalt Retires From Microsoft After 27 Years
content:
Dan Greenawalt, who founded Turn 10 Studios and led the creation of Forza, is retiring from Microsoft after 27 years. Trevor Williams, the head of Playground Games, told staff in an internal memo that The Verge’s Tom Warren reported on 29 October. “Dan Greenawalt has decided that this is the right time for him to retire from Microsoft,” Williams wrote, Shacknews reported . “It’s hard to overstate Dan’s impact over the past 27 years.”

He won’t leave straight away. Greenawalt will first advise Michel Bastien, Playground’s new chief operating officer, before he formally leaves the company. Williams thanked him in the memo for “his leadership, his support, and his partnership.”

Five weeks earlier, Xbox folded Turn 10, which is based near Seattle, into Playground Games, the studio in Leamington Spa, England, that makes Forza Horizon. The Redmond team now works as Playground Games Redmond and helps make Forza Horizon and Fable, Pure Xbox reported . Forza Motorsport, the series Greenawalt started, hasn’t had an update since 2025, and Microsoft hasn’t said whether it will get another game.

Greenawalt started at Microsoft as a test engineer on its early racing games, including Midtown Madness, RalliSport Challenge and Project Gotham Racing, according to The Drive . He founded Turn 10 inside Microsoft in 2001, the year the original Xbox launched. The first Forza Motorsport came out on the original Xbox in 2005. He directed it and the next three games, Forza Motorsport 2 in 2007, Forza Motorsport 3 in 2009 and Forza Motorsport 4 in 2011, which took the series through the Xbox 360 years. He later moved into a wider creative director role covering the franchise.

Turn 10’s ForzaTech engine, first built for those games, has run every Forza Horizon game since the first one in 2012, and it also powers Playground’s Fable, GTPlanet noted. Greenawalt didn’t direct Horizon himself, but the first Horizon was built on the technology and car content from his Motorsport games, The Drive pointed out.

Turn 10 kept releasing Motorsport games for another decade after he stepped back from directing them. Forza Motorsport 5 launched with the Xbox One in 2013, followed by Forza Motorsport 6 in 2015, the PC-only Forza Motorsport 6: Apex in 2016 and Forza Motorsport 7 in 2017. The most recent game, a reboot simply called Forza Motorsport, came out on Xbox Series X|S and PC in 2023.

title: Take-Two Files 16 Vice City Trademarks Three Weeks Before GTA 6
content:
Take-Two Interactive filed 16 US trademark applications on 28 October for Vice City, the city at the centre of Grand Theft Auto 6, and for related names. The game comes out on 19 November. The applications to the US Patent and Trademark Office cover everything from game software to lighters, and we found no earlier report of them.

Ten are for “Vice City” on its own, without the Grand Theft Auto name. Four are for “Vice City Leonida”, which pairs the city with Leonida, the fictional state GTA 6 is set in. The other two cover the Grand Theft Auto name and the Rockstar Games logo. Andrea L. Calvaruso of Kelley Drye & Warren, who handles Take-Two’s trademark filings, filed all 16, and each is waiting to be assigned to an examiner. The filings arrive three weeks before Take-Two’s most anticipated release in years, and they would protect the city’s name on its own, apart from the Grand Theft Auto brand.

The Vice City application for game software claims first use on 29 October 2002, the day Grand Theft Auto: Vice City came out in North America. A matching filing for online games and other entertainment services claims the same date. Both are use-based, so Take-Two is asking for registration on the grounds that it has used the name for 24 years.

The other Vice City applications fall in the classes for jewellery, printed matter, bags, housewares, clothing, toys and lighters. The trademark system sorts goods into numbered classes, and a mark only protects the classes it is registered in. Filing across this many is how a company makes sure a name is covered wherever it plans to sell it.

Several of the use-based filings give a much more recent first-use date. The Vice City clothing application, for shirts, sweatshirts, jackets and caps, lists 8 October 2026. So do the Vice City lighter filing, the Grand Theft Auto bags filing and the Rockstar Games filing for printed materials. That was the day Rockstar opened its GTA 6 collection on the Rockstar Store, with T-shirts, caps, canvas bags, a Vice City Zippo lighter and sticker sets.

TalkEsport has the full price list . Take-Two started selling the products first and filed for the trademarks three weeks later, citing the store launch as its first use. Take-Two filed the four Vice City Leonida applications on an intent-to-use basis, which means it hasn’t sold anything under that name yet. They cover sunglasses , bags, printed guides, and the class for jewellery and watches. The printed-guides filing lists “manuals, pamphlets, booklets, books, magazines, posters, stickers, and guides” about game strategy, wording broad enough to cover an official strategy guide.

title: LEC : Hype accepte de baisser son salaire pour rester chez Heretics

title: Fidelity Cuts Epic Games Valuation by 47% in a Year
content:
Fidelity has cut its valuation of Epic Games shares by 47% in a year, according to fund holdings reports filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission on 26 October. The asset manager now puts the Fortnite maker’s stock at $368.37 a share, down from $700.58 at the end of August 2025. When Fidelity first invested, in July 2020, it paid $575.

Fidelity holds Epic in several of its funds, and every report TalkEsport checked uses the same price for 31 August 2026. The largest stake we found sits in the Fidelity Growth Company Fund , which owns 51,800 Epic shares valued at $19.08 million. It paid $29.8 million for them. The Fidelity Advisor Equity Growth Fund bought later, in March 2021, at $885 a share, so its holding is now worth 58% less than it cost.

The decline has been steady. The Growth Company K6 Fund valued its Epic shares at $700.58 in its report for August 2025 , then at $510.41 in February. Fidelity’s semiannual report put them at $441.44 at the end of May, and the August figure is 28% below February’s.

Fidelity’s numbers trace a full round trip. The round it joined in 2020 raised $1.78 billion and valued Epic at $17.3 billion, Bloomberg reported at the time. In April 2021 Epic raised another $1 billion at a $28.7 billion valuation, with Sony putting in $200 million and Fidelity Management & Research again among the investors . A year later Sony and KIRKBI, the Lego family’s holding company, put in $1 billion each at a valuation of $31.5 billion, TechCrunch reported.

Disney’s $1.5 billion investment in February 2024 came at a lower price. Disney didn’t state a valuation, but Reuters, citing The Information, put the implied figure at about $22.5 billion and said Fidelity, T. Rowe Price and BlackRock had recently marked their Epic stakes at roughly the price Disney paid.

Fidelity’s mark is now 36% below what it paid in 2020. The filings don’t give a figure for the whole company, but one can be estimated. Disney paid $600 a share in 2024 in a deal that valued Epic at $22.5 billion, according to Forge , which tracks trades in private company shares. At that share count, Fidelity’s $368.37 mark works out to about $13.8 billion by TalkEsport’s calculation, down from roughly $26.3 billion a year earlier. The estimate assumes Epic hasn’t issued many new shares since then.
